## Overview

The system has a React/Vite client, Firebase Authentication, a Python/FastAPI service, and Google Cloud data/model services. FastAPI verifies Firebase ID tokens before profile, session, matching, or chat operations. The matching workflow retrieves indexed trial chunks from BigQuery, uses Google ADK and Gemini for structured extraction and assessment, verifies evidence in application code, and saves the validated query and full structured result to the owning user's Firestore session.

## High-Level Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    User[Clinical technician] --> Web[React and Vite]
    Web -->|Sign in| Auth[Firebase Authentication]
    Web -->|Bearer token| API[FastAPI]
    API -->|Verify token| Auth
    API -->|Profile session and chat| DB[(Cloud Firestore)]
    API --> Workflow[Validation and matching workflow]
    Workflow -->|Vector search| BQ[(BigQuery trial chunks)]
    Workflow -->|Structured model tasks| Model[Google ADK and Gemini]
    Ingest[ClinicalTrials.gov ingestion] -->|Chunk and embed| BQ
```

The browser obtains an ID token from Firebase and sends it to FastAPI. The API verifies the token, enforces UID/session ownership, calls the matching or chat workflow, and persists user data through Firebase Admin. Trial ingestion is an offline path independent of user requests.

The evidence dashboard summarizes validated search facts and criterion coverage across the returned shortlist. Criterion detail remains tied to verified trial quotes and supported patient evidence. Its print-ready HTML report is assembled in the browser on demand, includes official ClinicalTrials.gov links, and is not sent back to the API.

## Components

| Component | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| React/Vite workspace | Sign-in, case intake, trial shortlist, evidence traceability dashboard, trial detail, and follow-up chat UI. |
| Firebase Authentication | Email/password accounts and signed ID tokens. |
| FastAPI `main.py` | HTTP routes, CORS, request IDs, authentication dependencies, and error mapping. |
| `auth_dependency.py` / `firebase_auth.py` | Verify ID tokens and initialize Firebase Admin/Firestore access. |
| `user_data.py` | Store profiles, queries, full match results, and chat turns under a user's UID. |
| `pipeline.py` / `workflow.py` | Validate cases, apply urgent screening, retrieve candidates, assess criteria, and rank results. |
| `adk_runtime.py` / `tasks.py` / `tools.py` | Run constrained extraction, assessment, and chat model tasks with bounded retrieval. |
| `eligibility_judge.py` | Verify criterion quotes and calculate conservative verdicts in ordinary application code. |
| `chat.py` / `retriever.py` / `trial_store.py` | Retrieve evidence for allowed trial IDs and create cited responses. |
| Ingestion scripts | Fetch, normalize, chunk, embed, and load trial data. |
| BigQuery and Vertex AI | Store/search trial vectors and create embeddings. |

## Main User Flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    actor User
    participant UI as React client
    participant Firebase as Firebase Auth
    participant API as FastAPI
    participant DB as Firestore
    participant WF as Matching and chat workflow
    participant Cloud as BigQuery and Gemini
    User->>UI: Sign in or create account
    UI->>Firebase: Authenticate with email and password
    Firebase-->>UI: Return ID token
    UI->>API: Request profile with bearer token
    API->>Firebase: Verify ID token
    API->>DB: Read or initialize users/{uid}
    DB-->>API: Return profile
    API->>DB: List user sessions
    DB-->>API: Return session list
    API-->>UI: Return profile and session list
    User->>UI: Submit anonymized case
    UI->>API: POST /api/match with token and session ID
    API->>DB: Confirm session belongs to token UID
    API->>WF: Validate, screen, retrieve, and assess
    WF->>Cloud: Search BigQuery and call Gemini tasks
    Cloud-->>WF: Trial evidence and structured proposals
    WF-->>API: Quote-verified shortlist
    API->>DB: Save query, timestamps, matched IDs, and full result
    API-->>UI: Return up to three candidates
    User->>UI: Ask a question about selected trials
    UI->>API: POST /api/trials/chat with token, session, and trial IDs
    API->>DB: Verify ownership and session trial membership
    API->>WF: Retrieve selected-trial evidence and answer
    WF->>Cloud: Fetch evidence and call Gemini
    WF-->>API: Cited answer
    API->>DB: Save chat turn
    API-->>UI: Return answer and citations
```

The API checks token identity and session ownership before processing case matching or chat. Chat trial IDs must be part of that session's saved result. Model proposals are validated before they are returned or persisted.

## Business Logic

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Case[Anonymized case] --> Validate{Input checks pass?}
    Validate -->|No| Reject[Return validation error]
    Validate -->|Yes| Urgent{Urgent warning phrase found?}
    Urgent -->|Yes| Notice[Return notice without model or retrieval]
    Urgent -->|No| Extract[Extract structured facts]
    Extract --> VerifyFacts[Verify facts against case]
    VerifyFacts --> Retrieve[Retrieve candidate trial chunks]
    Retrieve --> Refine{No candidates or weak best score?}
    Refine -->|Yes| Optional[Allow one supported refinement]
    Refine -->|No| Cap[Deduplicate and cap candidates]
    Optional --> Cap
    Cap --> Assess[Assess candidates concurrently]
    Assess --> VerifyQuotes[Verify source quotations]
    VerifyQuotes --> Blocker{Verified blocking criterion?}
    Blocker -->|Yes| Excluded[Record verified exclusion]
    Blocker -->|No| Candidate[Rank non-excluded candidates]
    Excluded --> Result[Return evidence and uncertainty]
    Candidate --> Result
```

A request makes one initial retrieval and at most one validated refinement retrieval. Candidate count and assessment concurrency are capped. A verified blocking criterion excludes a trial; otherwise, supported evidence can yield `POSSIBLY_ELIGIBLE`, while no supported criterion evidence yields `COULD_NOT_ASSESS`. The application never treats retrieval similarity as eligibility probability.

## Data Model

```mermaid
erDiagram
    USER ||--o{ SESSION : owns
    SESSION ||--o{ MESSAGE : contains
    SESSION ||--o{ MATCHED_TRIAL : summarizes
    TRIAL ||--o{ TRIAL_CHUNK : indexed_as
    USER {
        string uid
        string email
        string display_name
        string role
    }
    SESSION {
        string session_id
        string title
        string status
        timestamp created_at
        timestamp updated_at
    }
    MESSAGE {
        string message_id
        string turn_id
        string role
        string content
        timestamp created_at
    }
    MATCHED_TRIAL {
        string nct_id
        string title
        string verdict
        string criterion_quotes
        float relevance_score
    }
    TRIAL {
        string nct_id
        string title
        string status
    }
    TRIAL_CHUNK {
        string chunk_id
        string nct_id
        string chunk_type
        string text
        vector embedding
    }
```

Firestore paths are `users/{uid}`, `users/{uid}/sessions/{sessionId}`, and `users/{uid}/sessions/{sessionId}/messages/{messageId}`. Each session stores its title, validated search query, `createdAt`, `searchedAt`, `updatedAt`, matched-trial IDs, complete structured matching result, and status. The result retains criteria assessments and evidence so a reopened session can be restored. Chat turns use deterministic message document IDs, so a retried chat request updates the same records instead of duplicating them. Sidebar listing returns a lightweight result preview; opening a session returns the full result and chat history. BigQuery stores trial chunks and embeddings. The diagram shows conceptual relationships, not a claim that each entity is a separate collection/table.

## Deployment

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Browser[Browser] -->|HTTPS| Frontend[Static frontend host]
    Frontend -->|Firebase web SDK| Auth[Firebase Authentication]
    Frontend -->|Bearer ID token| API[FastAPI service]
    API -->|Verify token| Auth
    API -->|Admin SDK and ADC| Firestore[(Cloud Firestore)]
    API -->|Vector search| BQ[(BigQuery)]
    API -->|Model calls| Vertex[Vertex AI and Gemini]
    Job[Trial ingestion job] -->|Write trial chunks| BQ
    Job -. Optional processed files .-> GCS[(Cloud Storage)]
```

This is the deployment shape supported by the code; no production hosting manifests are included. Use HTTPS, configure the production frontend origin in CORS, and grant the API service identity only the necessary Firebase/Firestore, BigQuery, and Vertex AI permissions. Deploy `firestore.rules`, which denies direct browser database reads and writes.

## Security

- Firebase ID tokens are required for profile, session, matching, and chat routes. Health and readiness routes remain public.
- The backend derives the UID from a verified token, scopes Firestore paths to that UID, and checks session ownership.
- Chat requests can use only trial IDs in the owned session's saved match result.
- The application role is fixed to `clinical_technician` by the backend.
- Firestore client rules deny direct browser access. Admin SDK writes rely on server credentials and API ownership checks.
- Token verification skips a per-request revocation lookup to reduce latency; a revoked token may remain accepted until normal expiration.
- Submitted, identifier-screened patient case narratives, match assessments, and chat turns are persisted under the owning user's session. Delete a session to remove its saved data. The identifier check is limited and does not provide comprehensive de-identification.
- Retrieved trial text and patient input are treated as untrusted. Retrieval is bounded; structured outputs and quotations are validated before final verdicts.
- Identifier screening and urgent phrase checks are limited safeguards, not comprehensive de-identification or emergency triage.
- No regulatory compliance certification is claimed. Results require qualified clinical review.

## Scalability

- Candidate assessment and final-result caps come from configuration; concurrent assessment is bounded by `ADK_CONCURRENCY`.
- Each model call and retrieval call has a timeout. The matching and chat workflows also have derived overall timeouts capped in code.
- BigQuery provides managed vector storage and search. Monitor query cost and latency when tuning `CANDIDATES_TO_RETRIEVE`.
- Ingestion is independent of request handling and can be scheduled externally; the repository does not include a scheduler or autoscaling configuration.
- User data is partitioned by Firebase UID. Session and message retrieval limits bound data returned to the client.
- Production still needs platform-specific autoscaling, rate limits, monitoring, deployment automation, and data-retention policies.

The mocked workflow latency regression test compares the same six delayed assessment calls at concurrency 1 and 6. A local run measured medians of 226.3 ms and 39.9 ms respectively. These values validate the concurrency change in a simulated workflow; they do not predict live model or BigQuery latency.

### Search request, in execution order

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    actor Technician
    participant UI as App.jsx
    participant Client as api.js
    participant Route as main.py /api/match
    participant Auth as auth_dependency.py + firebase_auth.py
    participant Store as user_data.py / Firestore
    participant Pipe as pipeline.py
    participant Flow as agents/workflow.py
    participant Search as retriever.py + embeddings.py
    participant Model as tasks.py + adk_runtime.py / Gemini
    participant Judge as eligibility_judge.py

    Technician->>UI: Enter anonymized patient case
    UI->>Client: matchPatient(case, sessionId)
    Client->>Client: Get Firebase ID token
    Client->>Route: POST /api/match + bearer token + request body
    Route->>Auth: Resolve authenticated Firebase UID
    Auth-->>Route: Verified user claims
    Route->>Store: Confirm session ownership or create session
    Route->>Pipe: Validate case and screen urgent warning signs
    Pipe->>Flow: run_workflow_async(case)
    Flow->>Model: Extract patient facts
    Model-->>Flow: Structured patient profile
    Flow->>Search: Search trial candidates
    Search-->>Flow: Ranked candidates and source chunk IDs
    Flow->>Model: Assess shortlisted trial criteria
    Model-->>Flow: Proposed criteria with quotes and explanations
    Flow->>Judge: Verify quotes and calculate conservative verdicts
    Judge-->>Flow: Validated criteria and verdicts
    Flow-->>Pipe: Structured trial matches and evidence
    Pipe-->>Route: MatchResponse
    Route->>Store: Save search text and complete result to owned session
    Route-->>Client: JSON response with session ID
    Client-->>UI: Restore/display matches and criteria
```

**Fastest trace for a search:** start at `App.jsx` â†’ `api.js:matchPatient` â†’ `main.py:match` â†’ `pipeline.py:run_async` â†’ `workflow.py:run_workflow_async` â†’ `tools.py:ApprovedTrialRetrieval.search` â†’ `retriever.py:retrieve` â†’ `tasks.py` / `adk_runtime.py` â†’ `eligibility_judge.py` â†’ back to `main.py` and `user_data.py` for session persistence â†’ `api.js` â†’ result components.

**Fastest trace for sign-in and history:** `AuthScreen.jsx` â†’ `AuthContext.jsx` â†’ Firebase Authentication â†’ `api.js` profile/session calls â†’ `main.py` auth/session routes â†’ `auth_dependency.py` â†’ `firebase_auth.py` â†’ `user_data.py` â†’ Firestore. The server UID comes from the verified token; the client does not select the owner UID.

# Code Guide

This guide explains where the main parts of the Clinical Trial RAG application live. The code is grouped by responsibility so a change to one feature does not need to be mixed into unrelated files.

## Application flow

1. The React app in `frontend/src/App.jsx` connects the workspace, sign-in state, active search session, and screen-level navigation.
2. Reusable UI pieces live under `frontend/src/components/`. Result cards and assessment details are under `components/results/`; session history is under `components/session/`.
3. `frontend/src/api.js` sends requests to FastAPI. `frontend/src/hooks/useSessionManager.js` loads and updates a user's saved sessions.
4. `backend/app/main.py` creates the FastAPI app, applies request middleware, and exposes API routes.
5. `backend/app/agents/workflow.py` coordinates patient parsing, trial retrieval, evidence review, and response creation.
6. Individual backend services live in `backend/app/services/`. Each service handles one responsibility such as chat evidence, authentication, trial storage, or eligibility assessment.

## Backend modules

| File | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `backend/app/main.py` | API setup, request middleware, health checks, and HTTP routes. |
| `backend/app/schemas.py` | Validated request and response data shapes. |
| `backend/app/config.py` | Environment-based application settings. |
| `backend/app/agents/workflow.py` | Runs the matching steps and combines their results. |
| `backend/app/agents/tasks.py` | Defines focused AI tasks and their instructions. |
| `backend/app/agents/tools.py` | Gives the workflow controlled access to trial retrieval. |
| `backend/app/services/patient_parser.py` | Extracts supported patient facts from the case text. |
| `backend/app/services/retriever.py` | Finds trial records relevant to a patient case. |
| `backend/app/services/eligibility_judge.py` | Checks criterion assessments and produces a cautious verdict. |
| `backend/app/services/chat.py` | Finds trial evidence and prepares cited answers to follow-up questions. |
| `backend/app/services/user_data.py` | Reads and writes user profiles, search sessions, results, and chat history. |
| `backend/app/services/firebase_auth.py` | Verifies Firebase identity tokens for protected requests. |
| `backend/app/services/safety.py` | Applies patient-data and clinical safety checks. |

## Frontend modules

| Folder or file | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `frontend/src/auth/` | Sign-in, account creation, and authenticated user state. |
| `frontend/src/components/layout/` | Shared page shell, header, footer, and welcome content. |
| `frontend/src/components/results/` | Trial results, criterion evidence, passages, and assessment summary. |
| `frontend/src/components/session/` | Session list, selection, rename, and delete controls. |
| `frontend/src/components/chat/` | Trial evidence chat UI. |
| `frontend/src/components/ui/` | Small reusable buttons, badges, dialogs, and loading states. |
| `frontend/src/hooks/` | Reusable stateful behavior such as session management and notifications. |
| `frontend/src/utils/` | Formatting, evidence report, deduplication, and browser storage helpers. |
| `frontend/src/api.js` | Authenticated communication with the backend. |

## Comment style

Comments explain why a decision exists or what a block is responsible for. Names and short expressions should explain ordinary code directly; repeating each line in a comment makes changes harder to maintain. Python functions use docstrings for their purpose, while JSX and JavaScript use short comments around non-obvious behavior or grouped sections.

## Safe change checklist

- Keep API request and response shapes in `schemas.py` and update both sides when a shape changes.
- Keep user-owned Firestore reads and writes scoped by the authenticated UID.
- Keep React view components focused on displaying data; move reusable state behavior into hooks and calculations into utilities.
- Keep trial eligibility language cautious and traceable to the evidence shown to the user.

========== FILE: firestore.rules ==========

rules_version = '2';
service cloud.firestore {
  match /databases/{database}/documents {
    // All application Firestore access goes through FastAPI's Admin SDK.
    // Client SDK access is denied; API routes enforce identity and ownership.
    match /{document=**} {
      allow read, write: if false;
    }
  }
}



========== FILE: README.md ==========

# Clinical Trial RAG

Clinical Trial RAG is a healthcare research-support application that helps a clinical technician or researcher compare a **de-identified patient case** with indexed clinical-trial records. It searches for relevant trials, shows the criteria and patient evidence it used, identifies missing information, and lets the user ask evidence-grounded follow-up questions.

> **Clinical safety:** The application is not a diagnostic tool and does not determine or confirm eligibility. Its results are preliminary research support. A qualified clinical team must review the official trial record and make any decision.

## Project summary for a presentation

| Topic | Explanation |
|---|---|
| Project | Clinical Trial RAG, a research-support application for reviewing trials against a patient case. |
| User | A clinical technician, researcher, or qualified clinical team member. |
| Input | A de-identified clinical summary with relevant demographics, diagnosis, biomarkers, measurements, treatment history, and other known facts. |
| Processing | Safety and input checks, fact extraction, semantic trial retrieval, optional bounded query refinement, criterion assessment, and evidence verification. |
| Output | A shortlist of trial records with source-linked criteria evidence, unknowns, and cautious preliminary verdicts. |
| Persistence | Firebase Authentication identifies the user; Cloud Firestore stores that user's sessions, results, and chat history. |
| Main value | Reduces manual searching and makes the reasoning easier to inspect by showing trial text, patient evidence, and missing facts. |
| Important limitation | A high topic-similarity score is not a probability of eligibility, and no perfect or validated overall accuracy percentage is claimed. |

### A short introduction to say to your manager

> â€œThis project helps research teams find clinical trials that may be relevant to a de-identified patient case. It searches trial records, compares a bounded set of criteria with the facts provided, and shows the supporting text and missing information so a clinical professional can review the official record. It is decision support, not an automated eligibility decision.â€

## Problem and solution

Trial records are spread across many study pages and their eligibility criteria are written as long text. Manually finding potentially relevant records and comparing each requirement with case details can take time. A simple keyword search can also miss trials that use different wording for the same condition or treatment.

This application combines **retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)** with deterministic application checks:

1. The search converts a de-identified case into supported facts and a semantic query.
2. Vector retrieval finds trial passages that are relevant in meaning, not only by exact keyword.
3. A language model proposes structured comparisons between case facts and trial criteria.
4. Application code checks the model's quoted text and calculates cautious labels.
5. The UI displays the evidence and unknowns so a person can review the result.

RAG means the model is given retrieved trial material to work from. The model is not expected to answer from memory alone.

## What the user can do

- Sign up or sign in using Firebase Authentication.
- Submit a de-identified patient case for matching.
- View up to the configured maximum of non-excluded trial candidates and separately listed trials with verified blocking criteria.
- Review trial status, phase, condition, match relevance, criteria, retrieved passages, and source links.
- Open a dedicated clinical assessment summary and filter criteria by status.
- See missing or conflicting facts that may need clarification.
- Save, reopen, rename, switch between, or delete personal search sessions.
- Ask follow-up questions grounded in the selected trials' evidence.
- Generate a print-ready report in the browser.

## How one search works

The steps below describe the actual request path.

1. **Sign in.** `AuthScreen.jsx` uses Firebase Authentication, and `AuthContext.jsx` tracks the signed-in user and profile.
2. **Load the user's sessions.** `useSessionManager.js` asks the backend for the user's sessions and restores the selected session.
3. **Enter a case.** The user submits a de-identified narrative in `App.jsx`. The frontend API client adds the Firebase ID token to the request.
4. **Authenticate and check ownership.** `main.py` receives `POST /api/match`; the auth dependency verifies the token. The backend uses the verified UID to confirm session ownership.
5. **Validate and screen.** `pipeline.py` checks the case length and common direct identifiers, then checks the configured urgent-warning phrases before model or retrieval work. The warning list is a limited phrase screen, not emergency triage.
6. **Extract facts.** `workflow.py` calls an extraction task defined in `tasks.py`. Gemini returns a structured profile; application code checks facts and handles conflicts or missing values.
7. **Retrieve trials.** `retriever.py` obtains a query embedding through `embeddings.py` and searches trial chunks in BigQuery. Candidate trials are deduplicated and ranked.
8. **Optionally refine search.** If no candidates are found or the best retrieval score is below the configured threshold, the workflow may propose one profile-grounded refinement and run at most one additional retrieval.
9. **Assess criteria.** A bounded shortlist is assessed. The model proposes criterion results and quotes from the supplied trial text and patient case.
10. **Verify evidence and determine labels.** `eligibility_judge.py` checks quotes in ordinary application code and computes conservative preliminary verdicts. Unsupported evidence is not accepted as fact.
11. **Save the result.** `main.py` stores the query and complete result under the authenticated user's Firestore session.
12. **Display results.** React components show trial details, criterion evidence, passages, and uncertainty. The user can then open the assessment page or ask an evidence-grounded follow-up question.

### Main backend decision path

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Start[De-identified case submitted] --> Validate{Input checks pass?}
    Validate -->|No| Error[Return validation error]
    Validate -->|Yes| Urgent{Configured urgent phrase found?}
    Urgent -->|Yes| Notice[Return safety notice; stop matching]
    Urgent -->|No| Extract[Extract and validate supported facts]
    Extract --> Retrieve[Search indexed trial chunks]
    Retrieve --> Refine{No candidates or weak best score?}
    Refine -->|Yes| OneMore[Optional one-time grounded refinement]
    Refine -->|No| Assess[Assess bounded candidate set]
    OneMore --> Assess
    Assess --> Verify[Verify quoted criteria and case evidence]
    Verify --> Verdict[Compute conservative preliminary labels]
    Verdict --> Save[Save result to owned Firestore session]
    Save --> Show[Display results, evidence, and unknowns]
```

## Autonomous agents and refinement

In this project, â€œagentâ€ means a focused model task invoked by backend code. The agents do not independently choose arbitrary tools or make an unchecked final decision. The backend defines each task, its input, its output schema, and what tools or evidence it can access.

| Agent task | Purpose | How the application constrains it |
|---|---|---|
| Patient fact extraction | Pull explicitly stated facts into a structured patient profile. | Structured output schema; facts are checked against the case; conflicts are handled by application code. |
| Search refinement | Suggest one improved search phrase when initial retrieval is empty or weak. | At most one additional retrieval; accepted terms must be grounded in validated case/profile facts. |
| Trial criteria assessment | Compare supplied case facts with supplied trial criteria and propose quotes and criterion states. | Trial/patient quotes are verified; unsupported proposals are dropped or marked unknown; code determines the final preliminary verdict. |
| Trial evidence chat | Answer follow-up questions using evidence for selected trial IDs. | Trial IDs must belong to the user's saved session; answer task receives retrieved trial evidence and should state when it is insufficient. |

The model has no arbitrary shell, filesystem, network, SQL, or cloud tools. Retrieval and persistence are implemented in backend services. Each model call uses a temporary ADK session; saved user chat is separate and stored in Firestore.

## How trial data gets into the system

Ingestion is an offline/admin operation; it does not run for every user search.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    CTG[ClinicalTrials.gov API v2] --> Fetch[fetch_trials.py normalize records]
    PMC[PubMed Central BioC API] -. optional enrichment .-> FetchPMC[fetch_pmc.py]
    Init[build_index.py initialize BigQuery dataset/table] --> Ingest[ingest.py]
    Fetch --> Raw[Raw/processed trial data]
    FetchPMC -. enrich .-> Raw
    Raw --> Chunk[chunker.py split records into passages]
    Chunk --> Ingest
    Ingest --> Embed[Vertex AI embeddings]
    Ingest --> BQ[(BigQuery vector table)]
    Ingest -. optional upload .-> GCS[(Cloud Storage processed JSON)]
```

1. `fetch_trials.py` requests study records from ClinicalTrials.gov and normalizes their fields.
2. `fetch_pmc.py` can optionally add publication information.
3. `build_index.py` initializes the BigQuery dataset/table. It is infrastructure setup, not a step that fetches trial data.
4. `chunker.py` splits trial text into retrieval-sized passages, including eligibility text.
5. `ingest.py` embeds new chunks, validates vector dimensions and required fields, avoids duplicate chunk IDs, and loads records into BigQuery. It updates a local chunk cache and can upload processed JSON to GCS when configured.
6. At runtime, the backend retrieves relevant passages from BigQuery and gets trial metadata from `trial_store.py` and processed files.

The project includes BigQuery setup/verification SQL in `backend/sql/`. An explicit `--refresh` ingestion can replace the configured chunk table, so only use it when a full re-index is intended.

## Results, evidence, and scores

### What the labels mean

| Label | Meaning in this application |
|---|---|
| `EXCLUDED` | At least one verified criterion is marked as a blocker. A qualified team should still verify it against the official record. |
| `POSSIBLY_ELIGIBLE` | Some criteria are supported and no verified blocker was found in the assessed subset. This does **not** mean eligible; other criteria may be missing or unassessed. |
| `COULD_NOT_ASSESS` | The available verified criteria do not provide supported evidence to make a useful preliminary comparison. |
| Criterion `UNKNOWN` | The specific criterion could not be assessed from the supplied case evidence. The UI displays this as â€œCould not assess.â€ |

The workflow assesses a bounded number of candidates and the model may not cover every criterion. Therefore, the app intentionally does not claim that a patient is eligible.

### Interpreting percentages

The percentage shown in the results is **retrieval/topic similarity**: how close a search query is to a trial passage in embedding space. It is not an eligibility probability, clinical confidence, or measured system accuracy. A larger similarity score does not mean a higher chance of trial enrollment.

For meaningful accuracy claims, the project needs an expert-reviewed test set of representative cases and criteria. Evaluate trial retrieval, criterion-level correctness, missed blockers, unsupported claims, and calibration separately. Do not call an unvalidated score â€œ95% accurate.â€

## Sessions and persistence

- Authentication is provided by Firebase Authentication.
- The browser sends the Firebase ID token to protected FastAPI endpoints.
- FastAPI verifies the token and derives the UID from its claims; the frontend does not choose the UID used for Firestore access.
- User data is stored under `users/{uid}`. Session documents live at `users/{uid}/sessions/{sessionId}`; chat messages are stored under the session.
- A saved session includes the query, title/timestamps, matched trial IDs, structured result/criteria evidence, status, and chat history.
- The sidebar lists recent sessions by latest update. Opening a session loads its saved search and result rather than starting a new match.
- Session creation, rename, deletion, and chat/result clearing are implemented by authenticated API endpoints.

## Security and responsible use

- Protected profile, session, match, and chat operations require a verified Firebase ID token.
- Firestore paths are scoped by the authenticated UID. Chat trial IDs must be part of that session's saved results.
- Browser Firestore rules deny direct client reads and writes; API-side Firebase Admin access uses Application Default Credentials or the Cloud Run service identity.
- Case intake screens for a limited set of direct identifiers (email, phone, and US SSN patterns). This is **not comprehensive de-identification**. Submit only appropriately de-identified case information.
- Configured urgent phrases are a limited screen, not a medical emergency detector or triage service. They can miss situations or trigger incorrectly.
- Retrieved records, patient cases, and questions are treated as untrusted data. Agent tools and retrieval scope are bounded by application code.
- Request logs are designed not to include patient narratives, extracted facts, search queries, prompts, or model responses.
- Search narratives and assessment results are persisted in user sessions and contain health-related information. Follow your organization's policies for authorization, retention, and access.
- The repository does not claim HIPAA/GDPR compliance or regulatory certification.

## Run locally

### Requirements

- Python 3.11 or later.
- Node.js 18 or later and npm (the Cloud Run deployment guide currently asks for Node.js 20+).
- Google Cloud project with BigQuery and Vertex AI access.
- Firebase project with Email/Password Authentication enabled and Cloud Firestore created.
- Google Cloud credentials with access to the configured cloud resources.

### 1. Configure and start the backend

From the repository root, in PowerShell:

```powershell
cd backend
py -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python -m pip install --upgrade pip
pip install -r requirements.txt
Copy-Item .env.example .env
```

Edit `backend/.env` with your project/resource settings. Authenticate locally with Application Default Credentials:

```powershell
gcloud auth application-default login
gcloud config set project YOUR_PROJECT_ID
```

Start the API from `backend/`:

```powershell
uvicorn app.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --reload --reload-dir app
```

### 2. Configure and start the frontend

In a second terminal from the repository root:

```powershell
cd frontend
npm install
Copy-Item .env.example .env
```

Set the Firebase web app values in `frontend/.env`. Start Vite:

```powershell
npm run dev
```

Open `http://localhost:5173`. API documentation is at `http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs`.

### 3. Prepare trial data when required

Run these commands from `backend/` when initializing BigQuery and preparing trial data:

```powershell
python -m ingestion.build_index
python -m ingestion.fetch_trials
python -m ingestion.ingest
```

Optional literature enrichment:

```powershell
python -m ingestion.fetch_pmc
```

Deploy `firestore.rules` to prevent browser-side Firestore access:

```powershell
firebase deploy --only firestore:rules
```

## Configuration

Backend settings are loaded from `backend/.env` or the process environment. Never commit real credentials, tokens, Firebase private keys, or production secrets. See [`backend/.env.example`](backend/.env.example) and [`frontend/.env.example`](frontend/.env.example) for the complete variable lists.

| Backend variable | Example/default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GCP_PROJECT` | Set to resource-owning project | Google Cloud project used for BigQuery, Vertex AI, and related services. |
| `FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID` | Firebase project ID | Firebase Admin token verification and Firestore project. |
| `GCP_LOCATION` | `us-central1` | Vertex AI and default BigQuery location. |
| `GEMINI_LOCATION` | `global` | Gemini serving location. |
| `BIGQUERY_DATASET` / `BIGQUERY_CHUNKS_TABLE` | `clinical_trials` / `trial_chunks` | BigQuery trial vector table. |
| `EMBEDDING_MODEL` / `EMBEDDING_DIM` | `text-embedding-005` / `768` | Embedding model and expected vector size. |
| `GEMINI_MODEL` | `gemini-2.5-flash` | Model used for structured agent tasks. |
| `CANDIDATES_TO_RETRIEVE` | `40` | Chunk retrieval limit. |
| `CANDIDATES_TO_JUDGE` | `10` | Maximum configured candidates for criteria assessment (hard application cap: 10). |
| `TOP_K_RESULTS` | `3` | Maximum non-excluded results returned (hard application cap: 3). |
| `ADK_CONCURRENCY` | `6` | Maximum parallel candidate assessments. |
| `ADK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `60` | Per-task/retrieval timeout basis; workflow timeout is derived and capped. |
| `GCS_BUCKET` / `GCS_PREFIX` | Optional / `clinical-trials` | Optional processed-data bucket and object prefix. |
| `CORS_ORIGINS` | Local Vite origins | Allowed frontend origins for FastAPI. |
| `PROCESSED_DIR` / `RAW_DIR` | Backend data folders | Optional local data directory overrides. |
| `LOG_LEVEL` | `INFO` | Backend logging verbosity; production debug logging should remain disabled. |

Frontend environment variables configure Firebase web app access and optional `VITE_API_BASE_URL`. The emergency phrase list is maintained in [`backend/app/urgent_signs.json`](backend/app/urgent_signs.json).

## Tests and build

Backend tests use mocks for cloud/model dependencies. Run from `backend/`:

```powershell
python -m pytest -q
```

Build the frontend from `frontend/`:

```powershell
npm run build
```

There is also a mocked concurrency timing test:

```powershell
python -m pytest -s tests/test_workflow.py::test_mocked_assessment_latency_improves_with_bounded_concurrency -q
```

A previously recorded local run measured six mocked 30 ms assessment calls at median 226.3 ms for concurrency 1 and 39.9 ms for concurrency 6. This is a simulated comparison, not a live Gemini/BigQuery performance result.

## Deploy to Cloud Run

The repository includes backend and frontend Dockerfiles and a deployment script. Deployment uses two Cloud Run services: FastAPI and the React static application. Read [`deploy/README.md`](deploy/README.md) for the full procedure and IAM setup.

In PowerShell from the repository root:

```powershell
./deploy/deploy-cloud-run.ps1
```

The script's default target is project `quiet-terminal-422106` in `us-central1`. It deploys the API, builds the frontend with the API URL, deploys the web service, and configures API CORS for the web origin. Set the Firebase web configuration in ignored `frontend/.env` before deployment. Set the backend resource project in ignored `backend/.env` as appropriate.

The Cloud Run runtime service account uses Application Default Credentials. Grant least-privilege access to Firestore, BigQuery, Vertex AI, and optional GCS in the projects that own those resources. Do not deploy service-account key files. After deployment, verify the printed web URL and `/api/ready` endpoint. Deployment and future code updates are documented in [`deploy/README.md`](deploy/README.md).

## Presentation walkthrough

Use this order for a short manager demonstration:

1. **Introduce the problem:** explain that trial criteria are lengthy and manual comparison against case details can be slow.
2. **Show sign-in and sessions:** explain Firebase authentication and that a technician can reopen their own saved searches.
3. **Submit a synthetic, de-identified case:** point out that the application asks for clinical details but should not receive direct identifiers.
4. **Explain the workflow while it runs:** the system validates and screens input, extracts supported facts, retrieves trial records, and may refine weak retrieval once.
5. **Open the result list:** explain that these are semantically relevant trial candidates and that the percentage is topic similarity, not eligibility probability.
6. **Open a trial assessment:** show exact trial criterion text, patient evidence, supported/blocking/unknown states, and missing facts.
7. **Ask a follow-up question:** show that the answer uses evidence from selected trial records.
8. **Reopen the session:** demonstrate persistence of query, results, criteria, and chat history.
9. **Close with limitations:** say that results are preliminary and must be checked against the official trial record by a qualified clinical team.

### Suggested closing statement

> â€œThe system is designed to make trial discovery and evidence review faster and more transparent. It does not replace clinical judgment. Its usefulness depends on current trial data, detailed de-identified case information, and human verification of the cited criteria.â€

## Known limits and next improvements

- **No perfect-answer claim:** clinical records may be incomplete, trial wording can be ambiguous, and extracted criteria may need interpretation.
- **No validated overall accuracy percentage:** build an expert-reviewed test set before advertising sensitivity, accuracy, or eligibility probability.
- **Bounded criteria coverage:** the workflow assesses a limited number of trials and may not assess every criterion in every record. Unknown information should remain unknown.
- **Retrieval score semantics:** similarity helps rank passages but is not a clinical probability. UI labels should keep this distinction explicit.
- **Trial freshness:** records and recruiting status change. Re-ingestion and official-record verification are needed; the app does not guarantee live status.
- **Identifier screening is limited:** pattern checks are not a complete de-identification solution.
- **Operational readiness:** production use needs organization-specific privacy/security review, monitoring, retention policy, backup/recovery, and clinical validation.

Recommended quality work is to assemble a de-identified, clinician-reviewed evaluation set and report retrieval quality, criterion-level agreement, blocker recall, unsupported-evidence rate, unknown handling, and score calibration as separate metrics.

# Architecture Diagram

This project is a clinical-trial matching application with a React browser interface and a FastAPI service. Its offline ingestion flow prepares a registry corpus for retrieval; at request time, the service combines vector search with evidence-constrained eligibility assessment.

## Application Architecture

<!-- mermaid-checked: no \n, no em-dash/en-dash, no {} in labels, subgraphs are id["label"], arrows are -->|"label"|, all subgraphs closed by end, ids unique -->
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph ClientLayer["Client Layer"]
        Researcher["Clinical researcher"]
        Browser["Web browser"]
        ReactUI["React trial matcher"]
    end
    subgraph ServiceLayer["Application Layer"]
        FastAPI["FastAPI REST service"]
        MatchFlow["Matching pipeline"]
        TrialStore["Trial data store"]
        IngestTools["Offline ingestion tools"]
    end
    subgraph GoogleAI["Google Cloud AI"]
        Gemini["Vertex AI Gemini"]
        EmbedModel["Vertex AI text embeddings"]
        VectorIndex["Vertex AI Vector Search"]
    end
    subgraph TrialData["Trial Data"]
        TrialJSON[("trials.json")]
        ChunkJSON[("chunks.json")]
        GCS[("Google Cloud Storage optional")]
    end
    subgraph Sources["External Sources"]
        CTG["ClinicalTrials.gov API v2"]
        PMC["NCBI PMC BioC API optional"]
    end

    Researcher -->|"enters anonymized case"| Browser
    Browser -->|"renders application"| ReactUI
    ReactUI -->|"POST /api/match"| FastAPI
    FastAPI -->|"validates and dispatches"| MatchFlow
    MatchFlow -->|"extracts profile and judges criteria"| Gemini
    MatchFlow -->|"embeds search queries"| EmbedModel
    MatchFlow -->|"searches recruiting trial chunks"| VectorIndex
    MatchFlow -->|"loads trial and chunk metadata"| TrialStore
    TrialStore -->|"local fallback records"| TrialJSON
    TrialStore -->|"local fallback passages"| ChunkJSON
    GCS -.->|"optional configured data source"| TrialStore
    CTG -->|"fetches recruiting study records"| IngestTools
    PMC -->|"optionally enriches publications"| IngestTools
    IngestTools -->|"writes normalized study records"| TrialJSON
    IngestTools -->|"writes chunk metadata"| ChunkJSON
    IngestTools -->|"creates vectors and upserts index"| EmbedModel
    IngestTools -->|"upserts trial vectors"| VectorIndex
    IngestTools -.->|"optionally uploads JSON artifacts"| GCS
    FastAPI -->|"returns ranked evidence and profile"| ReactUI
```

### Technology Stack Summary

| Layer | Technology | Version | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| Frontend | React and React DOM | `^18.3.1` | Browser interface, patient-case input, profile and trial result display |
| Frontend tooling | Vite and React plugin | `^5.4.0`, `^4.3.1` | Local development server and production asset build |
| Backend API | Python, FastAPI, Uvicorn | Python version not pinned; `0.115.*`, `0.32.*` | HTTP API and ASGI server |
| API models | Pydantic and pydantic-settings | `>=2.8`, `>=2.4` | Request validation, structured model responses, environment-backed settings |
| LLM | Google Gen AI SDK with Vertex AI | `>=1.20.0`; Gemini model configured as `gemini-2.5-flash` | Patient profile extraction and criterion-level assessment |
| Embeddings | Vertex AI text embedding model | `text-embedding-005`, 768 dimensions | Query and trial-text vectors |
| Vector retrieval | Vertex AI Matching Engine | `google-cloud-aiplatform >=1.80.0` | Recruiting-trial nearest-neighbor search |
| Object storage | Google Cloud Storage | `google-cloud-storage >=2.18.0`; optional | Optional remote storage for processed JSON artifacts |
| Local data | JSON files | N/A | Processed trial records and vector-index chunk metadata |
| Trial ingestion | ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 | API version 2 | Fetches recruiting study records |
| Publication enrichment | NCBI PMC BioC API | N/A; optional | Retrieves available open-access abstracts for trial references |

### Data Storage & External Services

There is no relational database in the inspected application. Trial records and chunk metadata are held in `backend/data/processed/trials.json` and `chunks.json`, cached in-process by the trial store, and optionally read from or uploaded to Google Cloud Storage when configured. Vector representations live in Vertex AI Vector Search, with embedding and generative-model requests sent to Vertex AI. The offline ingestion scripts fetch recruiting studies from ClinicalTrials.gov and can optionally enrich records with abstracts from the PMC BioC API.

### Key Architectural Decisions

- Separates offline corpus preparation and vector-index population from online request handling.
- Uses embedding-based retrieval with trial-level Reciprocal Rank Fusion, then performs evidence-based criterion assessment on only a configured subset of candidates.
- Validates model quotes against source text and calculates the final eligibility verdict deterministically; a request-level guard rejects likely identifiers before processing.
- Uses local processed JSON as the default data source and supports GCS as an optional configured source or artifact destination.

## Component Relationships

The request path starts in the browser, enters the FastAPI route, and is orchestrated by the matching pipeline. Patient parsing and trial judging use structured model output; retrieval embeds queries and resolves vector hits against cached trial/chunk metadata. The separate ingestion path fetches and shapes registry records, optionally attaches publication abstracts, creates chunks, and populates the same data and vector-index artifacts consumed by the online path.

<!-- mermaid-checked: no \n, no em-dash/en-dash, no {} in labels, subgraphs are id["label"], arrows are -->|"label"|, all subgraphs closed by end, ids unique -->
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph Presentation["Presentation"]
        cMain["main.jsx"]
        cApp["App.jsx"]
        cApi["api.js"]
        cProfile["ProfilePanel.jsx"]
        cCard["TrialCard.jsx"]
    end
    subgraph ApiLayer["API"]
        cFastAPI["main.py FastAPI routes"]
        cSchemas["schemas.py Pydantic models"]
    end
    subgraph Business["Matching Business Logic"]
```

### Component Inventory

| Component | Layer | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main.jsx` | Presentation | React entry point | Mounts the React application and global styles |
| `App.jsx` | Presentation | Page component | Captures case input, submits matching requests, handles loading/errors, and displays results |
| `api.js` | Presentation | HTTP client module | Sends the patient case to `/api/match` and parses the response |
| `ProfilePanel.jsx` | Presentation | React component | Displays structured patient facts returned by the API |
| `TrialCard.jsx` | Presentation | React component | Displays each trial match, verdict, criteria evidence, and retrieved passages |
| `main.py` | API | FastAPI application and routes | Configures CORS and exposes health and matching endpoints |
| `schemas.py` | API and contracts | Pydantic models | Validates the request and defines profile, criterion, trial-match, and response shapes |
| `pipeline.py` | Business logic | Request orchestrator | Applies the identifier guard, parses the case, retrieves candidates, judges trials, ranks results, and builds the response |
| `patient_parser.py` | Business logic | LLM adapter | Extracts explicitly stated patient facts and a condition-focused retrieval query |
| `retriever.py` | Business logic | Vector retrieval service | Embeds queries, filters vector search to recruiting trials, and fuses hits into trial-level candidates |
| `eligibility_judge.py` | Business logic | Evidence assessor | Assesses trial criteria, verifies quoted evidence against source text, applies structured age/sex checks, and computes verdicts |
| `embeddings.py` | Infrastructure | Embedding client | Batches, retries, and normalizes query or document embeddings |
| `trial_store.py` | Data access | Cached JSON data store | Loads trial records and chunk metadata from GCS when configured, otherwise from local processed JSON |
| `gcs_store.py` | Infrastructure | Object storage adapter | Uploads and downloads JSON artifacts in the configured GCS bucket |
| `fetch_trials.py` | Offline ingestion | Registry fetcher | Fetches recruiting trials from ClinicalTrials.gov and normalizes study fields |
| `fetch_pmc.py` | Offline ingestion | Publication enricher | Optionally resolves trial references and attaches available PMC abstracts |
| `chunker.py` | Offline ingestion | Text transformer | Splits trial overview and eligibility text into indexed chunks |
| `build_index.py` | Offline ingestion | Vector index builder | Embeds chunks, upserts index datapoints, writes chunk metadata, and optionally uploads JSON files |
| `trials.json` | Data | Processed trial corpus | Stores normalized study records and eligibility details used by the matcher |
| `chunks.json` | Data | Chunk metadata | Maps vector datapoint identifiers to trial identifiers, chunk types, and source text |

import logging
import truststore
truststore.inject_into_ssl()
from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware

from app.schemas import MatchRequest, MatchResponse
from app.services import pipeline
from app.services.trial_store import trials

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

app = FastAPI(title="Clinical Trial Matcher")
app.add_middleware(CORSMiddleware, allow_origins=["http://localhost:5173"],
                   allow_methods=["*"], allow_headers=["*"])


@app.get("/api/health")
def health():
    return {"status": "ok", "trials_indexed": len(trials())}


@app.post("/api/match", response_model=MatchResponse)
def match(req: MatchRequest):
    try:
        return pipeline.run(req.patient_case)
    except ValueError as e:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=str(e))
    except PermissionError as e:
        logger.error(f"Permission error during trial matching: {e}")
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=503,
            detail="Google Cloud access denied. Check BigQuery IAM permissions.",
        )
    except RuntimeError as e:
        logger.error(f"Runtime error during trial matching: {e}")
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=500,
            detail=f"Retrieval error: {str(e)}",
        )
    except Exception as e:
        logger.error(f"Unexpected error during trial matching: {e}", exc_info=True)
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=500,
            detail="Internal server error occurred while matching trials.",
        )

# backend/app/agents/workflow.py

import asyncio
import time
import uuid
from typing import Any, AsyncGenerator

from google.adk.agents import BaseAgent, SequentialAgent, ParallelAgent
from google.adk.agents import InvocationContext
from google.adk.events import Event, EventActions
from google.adk.runners import Runner
from google.adk.sessions import InMemorySessionService
from google.genai import types

from app.config import settings
from app.schemas import (
    PatientProfile,
    CriterionResult,
    Passage,
    TrialMatch,
    MatchResponse,
)
from app.services.patient_parser import parse_patient
from app.services.retriever import retrieve
from app.services.eligibility_judge import judge, compute_verdict
from app.services.trial_store import trials, chunks


DISCLAIMER = (
    "Research decision-support only. Not medical advice. All eligibility "
    "reasoning is limited to the supplied case and registry text; confirm "
    "with the trial's contacts before referral."
)

VERDICT_ORDER = {
    "ELIGIBLE": 0,
    "POSSIBLY_ELIGIBLE": 1,
    "EXCLUDED": 2,
}


def stage_event(ctx: InvocationContext, agent_name: str, state_delta=None):
    """Build a standard ADK event, optionally updating session state."""
    return Event(
        invocation_id=ctx.invocation_id,
        author=agent_name,
        content=types.Content(
            role="model",
            parts=[types.Part(text=f"{agent_name} completed.")],
        ),
        actions=EventActions(state_delta=state_delta or {}),
    )


class PatientParserAgent(BaseAgent):
    async def _run_async_impl(
        self, ctx: InvocationContext
    ) -> AsyncGenerator[Event, None]:
        case = ctx.session.state["patient_case"]

        profile = await asyncio.to_thread(parse_patient, case)

        # Keep ADK state JSON-serializable.
        yield stage_event(
            ctx,
            self.name,
            {"patient_profile": profile.model_dump(mode="json")},
        )


class TrialRetrievalAgent(BaseAgent):
    async def _run_async_impl(
        self, ctx: InvocationContext
    ) -> AsyncGenerator[Event, None]:
        profile = PatientProfile.model_validate(
            ctx.session.state["patient_profile"]
        )
        case = ctx.session.state["patient_case"]

        candidates = await asyncio.to_thread(
            retrieve, [profile.search_query, case[:2000]]
        )

        limit = max(0, settings.candidates_to_judge)
        candidate_records = [
            {
                "nct_id": candidate.nct_id,
                "rrf": float(candidate.rrf),
                "best_sim": float(candidate.best_sim),
                "chunk_ids": list(candidate.chunk_ids),
            }
            for candidate in candidates[:limit]
        ]

        yield stage_event(
            ctx,
            self.name,
            {"trial_candidates": candidate_records},
        )


class TrialEligibilityAgent(BaseAgent):
    """Evaluate one retrieved trial using the existing eligibility judge."""

    nct_id: str

    async def _run_async_impl(
        self, ctx: InvocationContext
    ) -> AsyncGenerator[Event, None]:
        case = ctx.session.state["patient_case"]
        profile = PatientProfile.model_validate(
            ctx.session.state["patient_profile"]
        )

        trial = trials().get(self.nct_id)
        if trial is None:
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"Retrieved trial {self.nct_id} is missing from trial storage."
            )

        criteria, summary, dropped = await asyncio.to_thread(
            judge, case, profile, trial
        )

        result = {
            "criteria": [
                item.model_dump(mode="json")
                if hasattr(item, "model_dump")
                else item
                for item in criteria
            ],
            "summary": summary,
            "dropped_unverified": dropped,
        }

        yield stage_event(
            ctx,
            self.name,
            {f"trial_judgement:{self.nct_id}": result},
        )


class ParallelEligibilityAgent(BaseAgent):
    """Run trial evaluations concurrently in bounded batches."""

    async def _run_async_impl(
        self, ctx: InvocationContext
    ) -> AsyncGenerator[Event, None]:
        candidates = ctx.session.state.get("trial_candidates", [])
        batch_size = max(1, settings.adk_concurrency)

        for start in range(0, len(candidates), batch_size):
            batch = candidates[start : start + batch_size]

            workers = [
                TrialEligibilityAgent(
                    name=f"trial_judge_{start + offset}",
                    nct_id=item["nct_id"],
                )
                for offset, item in enumerate(batch)
            ]

            parallel = ParallelAgent(
                name=f"parallel_trial_batch_{start // batch_size + 1}",
                description="Evaluate independent clinical trial eligibility.",
                sub_agents=workers,
                timeout=settings.adk_timeout_seconds,
            )

            async for event in parallel.run_async(ctx):
                yield event

        yield stage_event(ctx, self.name)


class FinalRankingAgent(BaseAgent):
    async def _run_async_impl(
        self, ctx: InvocationContext
    ) -> AsyncGenerator[Event, None]:
        state = ctx.session.state
        profile = PatientProfile.model_validate(state["patient_profile"])
        candidate_records = state.get("trial_candidates", [])
        all_trials = trials()
        all_chunks = chunks()

        evaluated = []

        for candidate in candidate_records:
            nct_id = candidate["nct_id"]
            raw = state.get(f"trial_judgement:{nct_id}")

            # Never infer eligibility if evaluation did not produce a result.
            if raw is None:
                continue

            criteria = [
                CriterionResult.model_validate(item)
                for item in raw["criteria"]
            ]
            verdict = compute_verdict(criteria)

            evaluated.append(
                (candidate, all_trials[nct_id], criteria, raw, verdict)
            )

        evaluated.sort(
            key=lambda item: (
                VERDICT_ORDER.get(item[4], 1),
                -item[0]["rrf"],
            )
        )

        matches = []

        for rank, (candidate, trial, criteria, raw, verdict) in enumerate(
            evaluated[: settings.final_results], start=1
        ):
            passages = [
                Passage(
                    chunk_type=all_chunks[chunk_id]["type"],
                    text=all_chunks[chunk_id]["text"][:700],
                )
                for chunk_id in candidate["chunk_ids"][:3]
                if chunk_id in all_chunks
            ]

            matches.append(
                TrialMatch(
                    rank=rank,
                    nct_id=trial["nct_id"],
                    title=trial["title"],
                    url=f"https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/{trial['nct_id']}",
                    status=trial["status"],
                    phases=trial.get("phases", []),
                    conditions=trial.get("conditions", [])[:6],
                    sponsor=trial.get("sponsor"),
                    locations=trial.get("locations", [])[:3],
                    relevance_score=round(candidate["best_sim"], 3),
                    verdict=verdict,
                    summary=raw["summary"],
                    criteria=criteria,
                    dropped_unverified=raw["dropped_unverified"],
                    passages=passages,
                )
            )

        response = MatchResponse(
            patient_profile=profile,
            matches=matches,
            disclaimer=DISCLAIMER,
            latency_seconds=round(
                time.time() - state["workflow_started_at"], 1
            ),
        )

        yield stage_event(
            ctx,
            self.name,
            {"match_response": response.model_dump(mode="json")},
        )


def build_workflow() -> SequentialAgent:
    """Build the request-independent ADK workflow."""
    return SequentialAgent(
        name="clinical_trial_matching_workflow",
        description=(
            "Parse a patient case, retrieve clinical trials, evaluate "
            "eligibility in parallel, and rank the results."
        ),
        sub_agents=[
            PatientParserAgent(name="patient_parser"),
            TrialRetrievalAgent(name="trial_retriever"),
            ParallelEligibilityAgent(name="eligibility_orchestrator"),
            FinalRankingAgent(name="final_ranker"),
        ],
        timeout=settings.adk_timeout_seconds,
    )


async def _run_workflow_async(patient_case: str) -> MatchResponse:
    app_name = settings.adk_app_name
    user_id = "clinical-trial-api"
    session_id = str(uuid.uuid4())

    # Request-scoped session service prevents cases from sharing session state.
    session_service = InMemorySessionService()
    await session_service.create_session(
        app_name=app_name,
        user_id=user_id,
        session_id=session_id,
        state={
            "patient_case": patient_case,
            "workflow_started_at": time.time(),
        },
    )

    runner = Runner(
        app_name=app_name,
        agent=build_workflow(),
        session_service=session_service,
    )

    message = types.Content(
        role="user",
        parts=[types.Part(text="Run the clinical trial matching workflow.")],
    )

    async for _event in runner.run_async(
        user_id=user_id,
        session_id=session_id,
        new_message=message,
    ):
        pass

    session = await session_service.get_session(
        app_name=app_name,
        user_id=user_id,
        session_id=session_id,
    )

    if session is None:
        raise RuntimeError("ADK workflow session was not found.")

    result = session.state.get("match_response")
    if result is None:
        raise RuntimeError("ADK workflow completed without a match response.")

    return MatchResponse.model_validate(result)


def run_adk_workflow(patient_case: str) -> MatchResponse:
    """Synchronous entry point for the existing synchronous FastAPI route."""
    return asyncio.run(_run_workflow_async(patient_case))
"""State keys and typed helpers for Google ADK session state."""
from typing import Any

# Standard session state keys
STATE_PATIENT_CASE = "patient_case"
STATE_PATIENT_PROFILE = "patient_profile"
STATE_SEARCH_QUERIES = "search_queries"
STATE_CANDIDATES = "candidates"
STATE_RAW_EVALUATIONS = "raw_evaluations"
STATE_VERIFIED_EVALUATIONS = "verified_evaluations"
STATE_FINAL_RESPONSE = "final_response"
STATE_EXECUTION_METADATA = "execution_metadata"


def get_state_value(state: dict[str, Any] | Any, key: str, default: Any = None) -> Any:
    """Safely get a value from state whether it is a dict or an ADK State object."""
    if hasattr(state, "get"):
        return state.get(key, default)
    if hasattr(state, "to_dict"):
        return state.to_dict().get(key, default)
    return default

"""Lifecycle callbacks and guardrails for Google ADK agents."""
import logging
import re
import time
from typing import Optional

from google.adk.agents.context import Context
from google.adk.events import Event

from app.agents.state import (
    STATE_PATIENT_CASE,
    STATE_PATIENT_PROFILE,
    STATE_CANDIDATES,
    STATE_VERIFIED_EVALUATIONS,
    get_state_value,
)

logger = logging.getLogger("adk.callbacks")

# PHI regex for privacy guardrail: SSN, email, phone numbers
PHI_PATTERN = re.compile(
    r"(\b\d{3}-\d{2}-\d{4}\b|[\w.+-]+@[\w-]+\.[\w.]+|\b\d{3}[-.\s]\d{3}[-.\s]\d{4}\b)"
)


def privacy_guardrail_before_agent(ctx: Context) -> Optional[Event]:
    """Guardrail callback: Validates input privacy before agent execution.

    Rejects any case text containing identifiable personal health information (PHI)
    such as Social Security Numbers, email addresses, or phone numbers.
    """
    case = get_state_value(ctx.state, STATE_PATIENT_CASE, "")
    if not case and ctx.user_content:
        # Extract from user_content parts if state is not yet populated
        case = "".join(p.text for p in getattr(ctx.user_content, "parts", []) if hasattr(p, "text"))

    if case and PHI_PATTERN.search(case):
        logger.warning(
            f"Privacy guardrail triggered: Identifiable PHI detected in session {ctx.session.id}. Aborting."
        )
        raise ValueError(
            "Possible identifiers (SSN / email / phone) detected. Please anonymise the case."
        )
    return None


def observability_before_agent(ctx: Context) -> Optional[Event]:
    """Logs operational metadata before agent execution.

    Never logs patient narrative, credentials, or sensitive health data.
    """
    agent_name = ctx.agent_name or "unknown_agent"
    session_id = ctx.session.id if hasattr(ctx, "session") and ctx.session else "unknown_session"
    logger.info(
        f"[ADK Invocation] Agent '{agent_name}' starting | Session: {session_id} | Invocation: {ctx.invocation_id}"
    )
    # Store start timestamp in custom metadata or telemetry context
    if not hasattr(ctx, "_start_times"):
        ctx._start_times = {}
    ctx._start_times[agent_name] = time.time()
    return None


def observability_after_agent(ctx: Context) -> Optional[Event]:
    """Logs operational duration and counts after agent execution."""
    agent_name = ctx.agent_name or "unknown_agent"
    start_time = getattr(ctx, "_start_times", {}).get(agent_name)
    duration_str = f"{(time.time() - start_time):.2f}s" if start_time else "N/A"

    state_dict = ctx.state.to_dict() if hasattr(ctx.state, "to_dict") else {}
    cands = state_dict.get(STATE_CANDIDATES, [])
    evals = state_dict.get(STATE_VERIFIED_EVALUATIONS, [])

    logger.info(
        f"[ADK Invocation] Agent '{agent_name}' completed | Duration: {duration_str} | "
        f"Candidates: {len(cands) if isinstance(cands, list) else 0} | "
        f"Verified Matches: {len(evals) if isinstance(evals, list) else 0}"
    )
    return None


def age_validation_after_parser(ctx: Context) -> Optional[Event]:
    """Validates extracted patient age against original narrative.

    An extracted age must literally appear in the source text to prevent
    hallucinatory age inference by language models.
    """
    case = get_state_value(ctx.state, STATE_PATIENT_CASE, "")
    profile_dict = get_state_value(ctx.state, STATE_PATIENT_PROFILE)

    if profile_dict and isinstance(profile_dict, dict):
        age_years = profile_dict.get("age_years")
        if age_years is not None:
            try:
                age_int = int(age_years)
                if not re.search(rf"\b{age_int}\b", case):
                    logger.info(
                        f"Parser guardrail: Age {age_years} not found verbatim in narrative. Setting to None."
                    )
                    profile_dict["age_years"] = None
                    ctx.state.update({STATE_PATIENT_PROFILE: profile_dict})
            except Exception as e:
                logger.debug(f"Age verification check exception: {e}")
    return None

"""BigQuery Vector Search Retriever for Clinical Trials.

Replaces Vertex AI Vector Search endpoint calls with Google Cloud BigQuery
VECTOR_SEARCH() exact cosine distance similarity search.
"""
from collections import defaultdict
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
import json
import logging
import math
from typing import Optional

from google.api_core import exceptions as gcp_exceptions
from google.cloud import bigquery

from app.config import settings
from app.services.embeddings import embed
from app.services.trial_store import chunks

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Reusable BigQuery client instance
_client: Optional[bigquery.Client] = None


def get_bigquery_client() -> bigquery.Client:
    """Lazily initialize and return the BigQuery client."""
    global _client
    if _client is None:
        if not settings.gcp_project:
            raise ValueError(
                "GCP project ID is not configured. Set GCP_PROJECT in backend/.env"
            )
        _client = bigquery.Client(
            project=settings.gcp_project,
            location=settings.bq_location,
        )
    return _client


def set_bigquery_client(client: Optional[bigquery.Client]) -> None:
    """Override the BigQuery client instance (useful for unit testing)."""
    global _client
    _client = client


@dataclass
class Candidate:
    """Trial candidate with fused relevance and evidence chunk IDs."""
    nct_id: str
    rrf: float = 0.0
    best_sim: float = 0.0
    chunk_ids: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)


def validate_embeddings(vectors: list[list[float]], expected_dim: int) -> None:
    """Validate vector dimensions, non-emptiness, and numerical values."""
    if not vectors:
        raise ValueError("Cannot perform vector search with empty vectors list.")

    for idx, vec in enumerate(vectors):
        if not isinstance(vec, (list, tuple)):
            raise ValueError(f"Vector at index {idx} must be a list/sequence of numbers.")
        if len(vec) != expected_dim:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Embedding dimension mismatch at index {idx}: expected {expected_dim}, "
                f"got {len(vec)}."
            )
        for dim_idx, val in enumerate(vec):
            if val is None or math.isnan(val) or math.isinf(val):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Vector at index {idx} contains invalid numerical value {val} at dimension {dim_idx}."
                )


def build_vector_search_sql(
    project_id: str,
    dataset_id: str,
    table_id: str,
    num_queries: int,
) -> str:
    """Construct a parameterized BigQuery VECTOR_SEARCH GoogleSQL query."""
    if num_queries <= 0:
        raise ValueError("num_queries must be greater than 0")

    # Construct the query table subquery with UNION ALL for batch queries
    subquery_parts = [
        f"SELECT {i} AS query_id, @q{i} AS query_vector"
        for i in range(num_queries)
    ]
    query_subquery = "\n      UNION ALL\n      ".join(subquery_parts)

    full_table_path = f"`{project_id}.{dataset_id}.{table_id}`"

    sql = f"""
SELECT
  query.query_id AS query_id,
  base.chunk_id AS chunk_id,
  base.nct_id AS nct_id,
  base.chunk_text AS chunk_text,
  base.chunk_type AS chunk_type,
  base.metadata_json AS metadata_json,
  distance
FROM VECTOR_SEARCH(
  TABLE {full_table_path},
  'embedding',
  (
    {query_subquery}
  ),
  query_column_to_search => 'query_vector',
  top_k => @top_k,
  distance_type => 'COSINE'
)
ORDER BY query.query_id, distance ASC
"""
    return sql.strip()


def execute_vector_search(
    client: bigquery.Client,
    vectors: list[list[float]],
    top_k: int,
) -> list[bigquery.Row]:
    """Execute VECTOR_SEARCH against the configured BigQuery table."""
    project = settings.gcp_project
    dataset = settings.bigquery_dataset
    table = settings.bigquery_chunks_table

    sql = build_vector_search_sql(
        project_id=project,
        dataset_id=dataset,
        table_id=table,
        num_queries=len(vectors),
    )

    query_params: list[bigquery.ArrayQueryParameter | bigquery.ScalarQueryParameter] = [
        bigquery.ArrayQueryParameter(f"q{i}", "FLOAT64", [float(x) for x in vectors[i]])
        for i in range(len(vectors))
    ]
    query_params.append(bigquery.ScalarQueryParameter("top_k", "INT64", top_k))

    job_config = bigquery.QueryJobConfig(
        query_parameters=query_params,
        default_dataset=f"{project}.{dataset}",
    )

    try:
        query_job = client.query(sql, job_config=job_config, location=settings.bq_location)
        rows = list(query_job.result())
        return rows
    except gcp_exceptions.NotFound as e:
        msg = (
            f"BigQuery resource not found: `{project}.{dataset}.{table}` in location "
            f"'{settings.bq_location}'. Ensure the dataset and table are created and populated. "
            f"Original error: {e}"
        )
        logger.error(msg)
        raise RuntimeError(msg) from e
    except gcp_exceptions.Forbidden as e:
        msg = (
            f"Permission denied accessing BigQuery table `{project}.{dataset}.{table}`. "
            f"Ensure your GCP credentials or Service Account has BigQuery Data Viewer and "
            f"BigQuery Job User roles. Original error: {e}"
        )
        logger.error(msg)
        raise PermissionError(msg) from e
    except gcp_exceptions.BadRequest as e:
        msg = f"BigQuery vector search query failed (BadRequest): {e}"
        logger.error(msg)
        raise RuntimeError(msg) from e
    except gcp_exceptions.GoogleAPICallError as e:
        msg = f"BigQuery vector search API call failed: {e}"
        logger.error(msg)
        raise RuntimeError(msg) from e
    except Exception as e:
        msg = f"Unexpected error during BigQuery vector search: {e}"
        logger.error(msg)
        raise RuntimeError(msg) from e


def fuse_and_deduplicate(rows: list[bigquery.Row]) -> list[Candidate]:
    """Process BigQuery vector search rows with Reciprocal Rank Fusion and NCT deduplication.

    For cosine distance, similarity is defined as max(0.0, 1.0 - distance).
    RRF score is calculated as 1.0 / (60 + rank) for the highest-ranking chunk
    of each trial per query.
    """
    if not rows:
        return []

    # Cache chunks locally in memory so pipeline.py can access text/type if needed
    try:
        chunk_cache = chunks()
    except Exception:
        chunk_cache = {}

    # Group rows by query_id
    grouped_by_query: dict[int, list[bigquery.Row]] = defaultdict(list)
    for row in rows:
        q_id = row.get("query_id", 0) if hasattr(row, "get") else getattr(row, "query_id", 0)
        grouped_by_query[q_id].append(row)

    candidates: dict[str, Candidate] = defaultdict(lambda: Candidate(nct_id=""))

    for q_id, q_rows in grouped_by_query.items():
        seen_trials_in_query: set[str] = set()

        for rank, row in enumerate(q_rows):
            cid = row.get("chunk_id") if hasattr(row, "get") else getattr(row, "chunk_id", None)
            nct = row.get("nct_id") if hasattr(row, "get") else getattr(row, "nct_id", None)
            chunk_text = row.get("chunk_text") if hasattr(row, "get") else getattr(row, "chunk_text", "")
            chunk_type = row.get("chunk_type") if hasattr(row, "get") else getattr(row, "chunk_type", "overview")
            distance = row.get("distance", 1.0) if hasattr(row, "get") else getattr(row, "distance", 1.0)

            if not nct or not cid:
                continue

            # Ensure chunk is available in chunks() cache for downstream passage extraction
            if cid not in chunk_cache and chunk_text:
                chunk_cache[cid] = {"nct_id": nct, "type": chunk_type, "text": chunk_text}

            # Convert cosine distance to cosine similarity
            # In BigQuery, COSINE distance = 1 - cosine_similarity
            similarity = max(0.0, 1.0 - float(distance))

            cand = candidates[nct]
            cand.nct_id = nct

            # Add chunk ID to evidence list if not already present
            if cid not in cand.chunk_ids:
                cand.chunk_ids.append(cid)

            # RRF score: count each trial once per query for its top-ranked chunk
            if nct not in seen_trials_in_query:
                cand.rrf += 1.0 / (60 + rank)
                seen_trials_in_query.add(nct)

            cand.best_sim = max(cand.best_sim, similarity)

    # Sort candidates by fused RRF score descending
    return sorted(candidates.values(), key=lambda c: c.rrf, reverse=True)


def retrieve(queries: list[str]) -> list[Candidate]:
    """Retrieve trial candidates matching the given patient queries using BigQuery VECTOR_SEARCH.

    Parameters:
        queries: List of query strings (e.g. [patient search query, case text]).

    Returns:
        List of Candidate objects sorted by RRF relevance descending.
    """
    valid_queries = [q.strip() for q in queries if q and q.strip()]
    if not valid_queries:
        logger.warning("Empty or whitespace-only queries provided to retrieve(); returning empty list.")
        return []

    # Generate embeddings using the existing embedding service
    vectors = embed(valid_queries, task_type="RETRIEVAL_QUERY")

    # Validate vector format and dimension
    validate_embeddings(vectors, expected_dim=settings.embedding_dim)

    # Get BigQuery client
    client = get_bigquery_client()

    # Execute search
    top_k = settings.top_k_chunks
    rows = execute_vector_search(client, vectors, top_k=top_k)

    # Fuse, deduplicate, and sort candidates
    return fuse_and_deduplicate(rows)
import json
from functools import lru_cache

from app.config import settings


def _load(name: str):
    """Prefer GCS when configured, fall back to local file."""
    if settings.gcs_bucket:
        try:
            from app.services.gcs_store import download_json
            return download_json(name)
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"GCS read failed for {name} ({e}); using local copy")
    with open(settings.processed_dir / name, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        return json.load(f)


@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
def trials() -> dict[str, dict]:
    return {t["nct_id"]: t for t in _load("trials.json")}


@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
def chunks() -> dict[str, dict]:
    return _load("chunks.json")

PHI = re.compile(
    r"(\b\d{3}-\d{2}-\d{4}\b|"
    r"[\w.+-]+@[\w-]+\.[\w.-]+|"
    r"\b\d{3}[-.\s]\d{3}[-.\s]\d{4}\b)"
)

ORDER = {
    "ELIGIBLE": 0,
    "POSSIBLY_ELIGIBLE": 1,
    "EXCLUDED": 2,
}


def run(case: str) -> MatchResponse:
    if PHI.search(case):
        raise ValueError(
            "Possible identifiers (SSN / email / phone) detected. "
            "Please anonymise the case."
        )

    return run_adk_workflow(case)
from typing import Literal, Optional
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field


class MatchRequest(BaseModel):
    patient_case: str = Field(min_length=40, max_length=8000)


# ---- patient profile (LLM-extracted, explicit facts only) ----
class PatientProfile(BaseModel):
    age_years: Optional[float] = None
    sex: Literal["MALE", "FEMALE", "UNKNOWN"] = "UNKNOWN"
    primary_conditions: list[str] = []
    comorbidities: list[str] = []
    current_medications: list[str] = []
    prior_treatments: list[str] = []
    key_findings: list[str] = Field(default=[], description="labs, staging, biomarkers, performance status")
    search_query: str = Field(description="Condition-focused retrieval query built only from stated facts")


# ---- judge output (LLM) ----
class JudgedCriterion(BaseModel):
    criterion_type: Literal["INCLUSION", "EXCLUSION"]
    criterion_quote: str = Field(description="Verbatim, contiguous text copied from the trial criteria")
    patient_evidence_quote: str = Field(description="Verbatim text from the patient case, or empty string")
    impact: Literal["SUPPORTS", "BLOCKS", "UNKNOWN"]
    explanation: str


class JudgeOutput(BaseModel):
    criteria: list[JudgedCriterion]
    summary: str


# ---- API response ----
class CriterionResult(BaseModel):
    source: Literal["TRIAL_TEXT", "STRUCTURED"]
    criterion_type: Literal["INCLUSION", "EXCLUSION"]
    criterion_quote: str
    patient_evidence: str
    impact: Literal["SUPPORTS", "BLOCKS", "UNKNOWN"]
    explanation: str


class Passage(BaseModel):
    chunk_type: str
    text: str


class TrialMatch(BaseModel):
    rank: int
    nct_id: str
    title: str
    url: str
    status: str
    phases: list[str]
    conditions: list[str]
    sponsor: Optional[str]
    locations: list[str]
    relevance_score: float
    verdict: Literal["ELIGIBLE", "POSSIBLY_ELIGIBLE", "EXCLUDED"]
    summary: str
    criteria: list[CriterionResult]
    dropped_unverified: int
    passages: list[Passage]


class MatchResponse(BaseModel):
    patient_profile: PatientProfile
    matches: list[TrialMatch]
    disclaimer: str
    latency_seconds: float
